headline: Nifty ran hard while the *broader market trailed*
subline: FIIs bought Rs 6,836.81 Cr while DIIs sold. Smallcap 250 rose just 0.42%.
hero_text: The frontline led. Nifty rose 1.58 percent and Midcap 150 gained 1.00 percent, while Smallcap 250 managed only 0.42 percent.

why.title: Foreign money poured back in
why.desc: FIIs were net cash buyers while DIIs sold on the day.

why.title: Wall Street gave a lift
why.desc: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq both closed higher.

why.title: More stocks rose than fell
why.desc: Advancers outnumbered decliners across the full market.

why.title: No single trigger stood out
why.desc: The rally came without a clearly named catalyst.

sector_reasons.FMCG: Nestle and Tata Consumer led the staples bid
sector_reasons.Realty: Ran with FMCG among the leaders
sector_reasons.Private Bank: Private lenders lifted the Bank Nifty
sector_reasons.Metal: Edged lower as the metal pack stalled
sector_reasons.Energy: ONGC slipped and held the space back

movers_note_gainers: BSE led at 5.03%, with Nestle and Tata Consumer next.
movers_note_losers: Power Grid fell most. SBI, ONGC and Infosys trailed.
watch_text: Nifty closed at 23,810.85, between the 23,700 put wall and the 23,850 call wall. Wednesday tests that range.
lessons: The top 50 ran ahead of the pack. 38 of 50 rose, but the whole market managed only 1.4 to 1.
PSU banks fell while private banks rallied. The bank trade split down the middle.
Staples led the board. Nestle and Tata Consumer sat in the top three gainers.
No headline catalyst showed up. A broad rally can run on flows and a mild global tailwind alone.
alert_text: Eurozone CPI flash lands at 19:30 IST and US ISM Services PMI at 00:30 IST. Coal India trades ex dividend.
cta_headline: A frontline rally. *Save it for Wednesday*.
cta_sub: Full wrap every evening. Next bell is Wednesday 4 November.
next_text: Wednesday 4 November opens after four straight up sessions for Nifty. Coal India goes ex dividend.
caption_a:
Nifty jumped 1.58% to 23,810.85, but Smallcap 250 managed only 0.42%.
FIIs bought Rs 6,836.81 Cr in cash while DIIs sold Rs 3,678.85 Cr.
FMCG led the sectors at 3.65%.
Watch: Eurozone CPI and the Coal India ex dividend on Wednesday.
